claim: R4-15 (a) made a field that takes its fallback at an absorb change nothing (V08 §3.5's diff, l. 1674-1683). But `digest` is pure and knows no carried state: its step 3 (l. 1605-1611) still fills an empty, negative, fractional or non-numeric `population` with its field-table fallback, which is the tier word's rung default, else the one-click default's 5 000 (§2.4, l. 637). The diff then compares nothing for that field. The epoch cadence reads the population separately: V08 §3.6 (3) (l. 1853-1867) folds an epoch 'at the first week the population leaves the last epoch's `populationTarget` ± 5 % (read from `populationHistory`; with none, at `W₁` when the new population is outside it)', and sets each target 'linear between the target at `W₀` and the new population at `W₁`'. Read as written, that 'new population' is the digest's fallback. So on a bound CITY of 20 000 whose dossier arrives with `population` emptied, a builder of §3.6 (3) folds an epoch at `W₁` toward 5 000, or, where the span crosses a year end (an ordinary sync after time passed), interpolates the year-end epoch's target toward the fallback. That is a silent fall the absorb rule forbids. A builder who reads §3.5 first takes the carried population, so the two readings differ. T-V8-61 (a)'s fixture is an absorb on `city-1` right after its creation, with no year end and no history, so the interpolation is untested. §3.17's rows name the absorb case without the cadence. The ladder router's own read is already settled (§3.17's village row, l. 2678).
required_change: 1. V08 §3.6 (3), after 'else linear between the target at `W₀` and the new population at `W₁`, rounded to a person', add: '— where this absorb's `population` took its field-table fallback (V08 §3.5's diff), the new population is the carried one wherever this step reads it (this linear target, and the crossing tested at `W₁` with no `populationHistory`), the digest's fallback value never entering an epoch's target or a crossing test; `populationHistory`'s readable entries date and size the crossings and targets as usual'. 2. V08 §3.17's 'the digest and the diff' row, after 'an absorb whose `population`, `name` or `tier` is empty or unreadable, or whose `institutions` is no list: the carried value kept, no change, noted `field_fallback` (V08 §3.5)', add '; and where such an absorb's span crosses a year end, the epoch there targets the carried population, no epoch folding toward the fallback (V08 §3.6 (3))'. 3. T-V8-61 (a), after 'and the next readable dossier absorbs as usual', add '; on `city-1` an absorb whose `population` is emptied and whose present week lies past the next year end, with no `populationHistory` entry after the last epoch, folds the one year-end epoch with the carried population as its `populationTarget` and no epoch at `W₁`, the households unchanged by the fallback'.

claim: V08 §3.5's new absorb rule (R4-15 (a)) holds the carried fact for 'a field that takes its field-table fallback (V08 §2.4) — its path absent, or its value of no form its row reads'. The field table routes record sub-fields through the same fallback cells. The `institutions[]` row says 'a record's own absent field takes its row's `else` (V08 §2.6)', and its paths list `status`, `inactive`, `worldPulseFate`, `remnantReason` and `impairments[]`. The `activeConditions[]` row says 'a missing `label` no name, a missing `duration` no `untilWeek`, a missing `sourceEventType` the `archetype` row'. The rule does not say whether it reaches inside a record. Read literally, an institution whose record drops a current-only stamp keeps its carried `fate` and `inactive`; SettlementForge's entity stamps (`worldPulseFate`, `remnantReason`, the `…ByEventId` stamps) are 'per entity, current only' (research/sf/dossier-generation.md l. 864). With the diff's 'fates first' (§3.5's institution row; §7.7 item 14), a record SettlementForge reopens (F6: 'status back to `active`', research/sf/mapping.md l. 628) then stays closed on the map. Its cleared impairments and a condition's dropped `duration` also stay as carried. Read as top-level paths only, the record's `else` is compared as before round 4 and the institution reopens. Two builders build different absorbs on the reopen path. R4-15 (a)'s reason ('on a map made without a dossier nothing moves the population, the name, the tier or the institutions') concerns the dossier's own fields, not a readable record's optional parts.
required_change: V08 §3.5's diff, after '— makes no change: the carried fact stands.': add 'A field here is a row's own path — a top-level key, or a whole list; inside a record the digest reads (an institution, power, notable, condition, calamity or tradition), a sub-field absent or unreadable takes its row's reading (an institution field's `else`, V08 §2.6; the `activeConditions[]` row's missing `label`, `duration` and `sourceEventType`) at an absorb as at a creation and is compared as read, so a record follows what the dossier now says of it (an institution SettlementForge reopens, `status` `active` and its `worldPulseFate` gone, reopens, F6).' V08 §2.4's table lead: 'at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing,' → 'at an absorb a field that takes its fallback changes nothing, the carried fact standing — a row's own path; a record's absent or unreadable sub-field is read by its row and compared (V08 §3.5) —,'. T-V8-61 (a) adds: 'an absorb on `town-1` whose ruined or remnant institution record returns with `status` `active` and no `worldPulseFate` reopens it (F6), and one whose condition drops `duration` clears its `untilWeek`'.

claim: Round 4 made a late arrival a defined case for a calamity only (V08 §3.6 (3) under R4-08; T-V8-49 (g)). Its F5 targets' dossier events 'ride that epoch with it', with no week stated; the calamity's own entry sits at `W₀` + 1. Every other newly carried element change dated at or before `W₀`, in an absorb whose `W₁` is after `W₀`, has no stated week. §3.6 (6) folds element events 'at their week, between the epochs of (3)', but such a week lies before the last epoch, which is already in the log. §7.7 item 6 has the change mutate 'the map the last epoch left', and §4.11 *The clock* (1) takes the document's current week from 'the last folded event that carries one'. So an absorb whose last event is such a change (its present week coming from a tick already carried) moves the drawn week back before the last epoch: the season and every Works stage begun since then are drawn as of an earlier week. The degenerate row (`W₁` not after `W₀`) applies such changes finished. The case where `W₁` is after `W₀` has no outcome and no test (principle (11)).
required_change: V08 §3.6 (6), after 'undated ones follow the last epoch, applied finished (no Works).': add 'A newly carried change dated at or before the last epoch's week `W₀` folds after the last epoch at `W₀` + 1, applied finished (no Works), its own tick kept in its receipt and noted by `unreceipted_change`'s `late` variant — never at a week before the last epoch's, so §4.11 *The clock* (1)'s current week never falls back; a late calamity's F5 targets' dossier events ride that calamity's epoch in its `EpochInputs.dossier` at `W₀` + 1 ((3)).' V08 §3.6 (3)'s calamities parenthesis: 'its F5 targets' dossier events riding that epoch with it, above' → 'its F5 targets' dossier events riding that epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` with it at `W₀` + 1, (6)'. V08 §4.6's `unreceipted_change` row: 'for a calamity carried at or before the last epoch's week by an absorb whose week is not after it (V08 §3.6 (3); V08 §3.17)' → 'for a change carried at or before the last epoch's week (V08 §3.6 (3), (6); V08 §3.17)'. §3.17's 'changes to events and epochs' row adds to its degenerate inputs: 'a newly carried non-calamity change dated at or before `W₀`, `W₁` after it: folded at `W₀` + 1, applied finished, noted `late`'. T-V8-49 (g) adds that case, asserting that the document's current week after the absorb is not before `W₀`.

claim: V08 ## 6's catch-up batch row has three imprecisions in its new text. (a) The batch is 'the dossier events one epoch's span holds — dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week]', but an event dated at the epoch's own week rides that epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` (V08 §3.6 (6); §7.7 item 6) and is never a standalone event of the pass. (b) 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms and ≤ 3.5 ms' leaves the rung of each implicit; V06 §6.8 (1) states it (3 ms at TOWN and CITY, 3.5 ms at METROPOLIS). (c) 'one of T-V6-24's fixtures doing so fails the release' can be read to include T-V6-24's fourth catch-up fixture (100 years carrying 5 000 at the METROPOLIS cap). That fixture is built to pass the budget, and its bar is the one-epoch fold reported F-BUDGET-TIME; V06 §6.8 (6) says 'one of T-V6-24's three catch-up fixtures'. Each point is cited to the text that settles it.
required_change: V08 ## 6's 'an absorb with epochs' row: (a) 'dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week]' → 'dated in (the previous epoch's week, its week) — one dated at the epoch's own week riding its `EpochInputs.dossier` (V08 §3.6 (6))'; (b) 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms and ≤ 3.5 ms, averaged' → 'plus per event ≤ 3 ms at TOWN and CITY and ≤ 3.5 ms at the METROPOLIS cap, averaged'; (c) 'one of T-V6-24's fixtures doing so fails the release' → 'one of those three fixtures doing so fails the release (T-V6-24's over-budget fixture, 100 years carrying 5 000 at the cap, takes that one-epoch fold reported F-BUDGET-TIME by design)'.

claim: V08 §7.1's crisis fixtures sentence (l. 3222–3224), written this round for VV1112-r3-03, stages the simultaneous siege, quarantine and refugee week "on `city-1` and on `metropolis-3`". V12, its only reader, measures that week at the METROPOLIS cap: §3.15.12's fixture sentence (l. 2690–2692: "one week in which a siege, a quarantine and a refugee wave stand at once at CITY and at the METROPOLIS cap") and T122-6's bullet (l. 2712–2719: "on the week standing a siege, a quarantine and a refugee wave at once at CITY and at the METROPOLIS cap"); `crisis.share` is the only bar that reads several camp looks at once (a preview draws one look). The cap is 120 000 people (base §1.1, l. 395; §12.2's row, l. 16896). `metropolis-3` holds 45 824 (the frozen fixture; research/sf/PLAN.md l. 406; §13.2 lists it among the totality-only files, l. 18251), a METROPOLIS map far below the cap. V08 names no mutation to the cap, although it names one wherever it moves a fixture's population (T-V8-36's "`city-1` mutated to 8 000 people"; the force fixtures "each at TOWN, CITY and the METROPOLIS cap"). So the cap run of `crisis.share` has no producing fixture. One builder runs it on `metropolis-3` at 45 824 and reports the cap clause met; another stops, finding no cap fixture. The outskirts' sharing at the largest frame goes untested (principle (11): the maximum and the caps). The defect is in this lane's round-3 required text, which named `metropolis-3`.
